answer: Clone mills cannot keep a live well watch. A joiner stakes 9.60 POA and claims one ivory bead etched with a 22-byte well-id mixed from the epoch seed and a 40-bit lottery drawn 16 minutes earlier. They must reach the published oasis well, stand at a surveyed vertex marked by two non-kin witnesses, and drop five 6-byte depth pings 70 seconds apart; each echo must return within 2.4s and match the bead hash. Cost: 9.60 POA plus the wait and five live pings. A reused bead, missed echo, or a second claimant at that vertex burns 66% and dry-docks the well for nine epochs.
